Interim Financial Statements for the Quarter ended 30th June 2026

financials_interim.notes: SINGLE-ENTITY filer (Industrial Asphalts (Ceylon) PLC has no subsidiaries; only one column of figures is presented throughout, headed simply 'the Company') -- stored as GROUP basis per project convention for single-entity filers. Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026) vs Q1 FY2025/26 (three months ended 30 June 2025) comparative, both explicitly presented side-by-side on the face P&L (page 3) -- a genuine same-quarter YoY compare. NOTE ON BUSINESS MODEL: IAC's former asphalt-manufacturing operations have ceased; it is now effectively a property/investment holding company. 'Revenue' (Note 4, page 7) = Rent Income from Investment Property (Rs.11,704k) + Interest Income on short-term investments (Rs.901k) + Dividend Income (Rs.0k, 2025: Rs.1,308k) = Rs.12,605k, down 9.0% YoY (2025: Rs.13,858k) -- the fall is entirely due to zero dividend income this quarter (2025: Rs.1,308k) and a 33.5% drop in interest income (Rs.901k vs Rs.1,355k), which together outweighed 4.5% growth in rent income (Rs.11,704k vs Rs.11,195k). operating_profit=17,971 is the filing's own 'Profit/(Loss) from Operating Activities' subtotal (page 3); IMPORTANT CAVEAT -- unlike a normal operating-profit line, this subtotal already nets in Realized Loss on Financial Asset at FVTPL (Rs.3,742k, 2025: Rs.614k loss) and Unrealized Gain on Financial Asset at FVTPL (Rs.23,232k, 2025: Rs.10,880k), i.e. mark-to-market swings on the Company's investment portfolio, not operating trade income -- this is why operating_profit (Rs.17,971k) and profit_after_tax (Rs.16,186k) both EXCEED revenue (Rs.12,605k), producing >100% operating/net margins that are a genuine feature of this filing's presentation, not a data-entry error. Net FVTPL gain (realized + unrealized) was Rs.19,490k in Q1 FY26/27 vs Rs.10,266k in Q1 FY25/26, +89.9% YoY, and is the dominant driver of the 323% PAT growth. Net Finance Income/(Charges) is disclosed only as a net line (Rs.1,651k charge, 2025: Rs.3,099k charge) -- no gross finance_income/finance_costs split given, so those two optional fields are left blank rather than guessed. tax_expense=134 (page 3, 'Tax (Expense)/Reversal', stored as positive magnitude per project convention); profit_before_tax (16,319) - tax_expense (134) = 16,185 vs disclosed profit_after_tax 16,186 -- ties to within Rs.1k rounding. eps_basic=eps_diluted=0.004 (2025: 0.001) is the filing's only EPS line (page 3, 'Diluted and Basic Earnings/(Loss) per Ordinary Share', identical for both). Cross-check: profit_after_tax (16,186,000) / shares_in_issue (3,749,411,250) = Rs.0.00432/share, consistent with the disclosed Rs.0.004 (3dp rounding). Balance sheet (page 4) comparative column is 31.03.26 (FY start), NOT 30.06.25 -- normal LKAS 34 presentation, but it means no YoY balance-sheet comparison is possible from this filing (see gaps_note on the interim_updates row). total_assets=1,619,789 dominated by Investment Property Rs.1,447,000k (89% of assets) -- see Note 5: two competing valuations exist for this property (Rs.1,850,000k on an effectively-freehold basis by N.A.A.D. Siri Nissanka vs Rs.1,447,000k on a leasehold basis, remaining term 57.21 years, by KPMG); the Board adopted the more conservative KPMG leasehold figure. trade_receivables and trade_payables left BLANK: the Company has no trade operations, so 'Receivables and Prepayments' (Rs.46,652k, Note 6, page 7) is not a trade receivable -- it is dominated by a Rs.45,875k advance to Executive Director Mr. G Ramanan under a value-creation incentive scheme tied to monetising the Investment Property (a disclosed related-party item, not trade debt), and 'Other Payables' (Rs.6,919k) is not itemised as trade. inventory left blank -- none disclosed (no trading/manufacturing stock on this balance sheet). short_term_borrowings=429 = Bank Overdraft (the only interest-bearing/borrowing-like current item); long_term_borrowings left blank -- the only non-current liability of that character is Lease Liabilities (Rs.9,151k), a lease not a loan, so it is not counted as borrowings. capex=0 (2026 quarter; 2025 comparator was Rs.1,893k of PPE additions, not stored as this table holds only the current period). cash_from_operations=-8,424 (2025: -98,228, a large prior-year working-capital swing in equity-investment receivables/payables that reversed this quarter). shares_in_issue=3,749,411,250, unchanged YoY (Director/Shareholder tables, page 9-10). MATERIAL SUBSEQUENT EVENT (Note 9, page 8, after 30 June 2026 quarter-end, so NOT reflected in these figures): Executive Director Mr. G Ramanan signed a binding SPA on 7 July 2026 to sell 1,800,693,010 shares (48.03% of the Company, his entire stake) to Arcasia Investment & Trading (Pvt) Ltd and ATX Partners (Pvt) Ltd; a mandatory Rule 9 tender offer to all shareholders at Rs.0.40/share was approved by the SEC and announced on 24 July 2026 -- a change-of-control event highly relevant to interpreting this filing but outside the reported financial period.

thesis.thesis_text: Industrial Asphalts (Ceylon) PLC has ceased its former asphalt-manufacturing operations and is now effectively an investment/property holding company: 89% of its Rs.1,619.8mn of assets is a single investment property (carried at a conservative Rs.1,447.0mn KPMG leasehold valuation versus an alternative Rs.1,850.0mn freehold valuation obtained but not adopted), plus a portfolio of financial assets at FVTPL. Q1 FY2026/27 revenue (rent + interest + dividend income) fell 9.0% YoY to Rs.12.6mn, while PAT rose 323% to Rs.16.2mn -- but that swing is almost entirely a Rs.19.5mn net mark-to-market gain on the FVTPL portfolio, dwarfing the entire revenue base, not an operating improvement. More materially, on 7 July 2026 (after the quarter-end) Executive Director G. Ramanan signed a binding agreement to sell his entire 48.03% stake, triggering an SEC-approved mandatory tender offer to all shareholders at Rs.0.40/share -- 33% below the current Rs.0.60 market price, a material disconnect this thesis flags as the dominant near-term consideration (Q1 FY2026/27 filing, source_doc_id 52768).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no macro/real-estate-market data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Confidence is severely limited: only ONE interim quarter is on file (no annual report review, no multi-period trend), no dividend data exists, and a material subsequent event (change of control, 48.03% stake sale, SEC-approved tender offer at Rs.0.40/share) occurred after the reporting period and is not reflected in these financials at all -- the historical numbers analysed here may have limited relevance to the Company's near-term trajectory under new ownership.

financial_quality.rationale: Balance sheet is low-levered (short-term borrowings of only Rs.429k against total assets of Rs.1,619.8mn), and Total Equity of Rs.1,481.9mn is comfortably positive. However, earnings quality is poor: PAT of Rs.16.2mn is dominated by a Rs.19.5mn net mark-to-market gain on Financial Assets at FVTPL, not operating cash generation -- operating cash flow was a Rs.8.4mn outflow this quarter. This is not a going operating business generating sustainable financial-statement-quality earnings.

growth_outlook.rationale: Revenue (rent + interest + dividend income) fell 9.0% YoY to Rs.12.6mn, driven by the loss of Rs.1.31mn of dividend income and a 33.5% drop in interest income, partially offset by 4.5% rental growth. The 323% PAT growth is not an organic growth signal -- it is a non-recurring FVTPL mark-to-market swing (Rs.19.5mn net gain vs Rs.10.3mn a year earlier) that dwarfs the entire revenue base and provides no visibility into a sustainable growth trajectory for this now-dormant former manufacturer.

valuation.rationale: At Rs.0.60 (2026-08-28), annualising Q1 FY2026/27 EPS of Rs.0.004 (x4 = Rs.0.016) implies a run-rate P/E of ~37.5x on inherently volatile, non-operating earnings -- not a meaningful multiple. NAV/share (Total Equity Rs.1,481,930k / 3,749,411,250 shares) is ~Rs.0.40, so P/B is ~1.52x. Most materially, on 7 July 2026 the controlling Executive Director signed a binding agreement to sell his entire 48.03% stake, triggering an SEC-approved mandatory tender offer to ALL shareholders at Rs.0.40/share (approved 24 July 2026) -- 33% below the current Rs.0.60 market price. This project cannot explain why the market trades at a premium to the deal price that just set the terms of a controlling-stake sale, which is the dominant valuation signal here, not the FVTPL-driven EPS.

business_quality.rationale: IAC's former asphalt-manufacturing operations have ceased entirely; it is now effectively an investment/property holding shell whose only substantive asset is a single investment property (89% of total assets, carried at a conservative Rs.1,447.0mn KPMG leasehold valuation versus an alternative Rs.1,850.0mn freehold valuation obtained but not adopted) plus a trading portfolio of FVTPL securities. There is no diversified operating business to assess for franchise quality, and the imminent change of control adds significant strategic uncertainty.

governance_risk.rationale: No circulars/disclosures feed exists to independently verify this event, but the filing itself discloses a major governance-relevant subsequent event: the controlling Executive Director's binding sale of his entire 48.03% stake and the SEC-approved mandatory Rule 9 tender offer at Rs.0.40/share. The filing also discloses a Rs.45.9mn advance to the same Executive Director under a 'value-creation incentive scheme' tied to monetising the investment property -- a related-party item that, combined with the imminent ownership change, materially increases governance uncertainty even though nothing improper is alleged.

key_reasons: 323% YoY PAT growth to Rs.16.2mn is almost entirely a Rs.19.5mn net mark-to-market gain on the FVTPL investment portfolio, not operating improvement -- core revenue (rent, interest, dividends) actually fell 9.0% YoY

The stock trades at Rs.0.60 versus a Rs.0.40/share mandatory tender offer price approved by the SEC on 24 July 2026 following the controlling shareholder's binding sale of his 48.03% stake -- a 50% premium to the deal price that this thesis cannot explain from the financials alone

Balance sheet is low-levered (short-term borrowings of only Rs.0.4mn) and asset-backed by a single investment property carried at a conservative valuation, but earnings quality is poor: profit is structurally dependent on volatile FVTPL swings rather than a going operating business
watch_factors: Market price (Rs.0.60) trades well above the Rs.0.40/share mandatory tender offer -- either the market expects a competing/higher offer, is mispricing the change-of-control event, or is pricing in the investment property's alternative Rs.1,850.0mn freehold valuation; this project has no way to distinguish between these

The new controlling shareholders' (Arcasia Investment & Trading, ATX Partners) intentions for the Company -- continue as an investment holding vehicle, monetise the investment property, or pursue a new operating strategy -- are not disclosed in this filing and are the single biggest unknown for this stock
Realized losses on the FVTPL portfolio widened to Rs.3.74mn (from Rs.0.61mn) even as unrealized gains grew -- a portfolio showing more volatility, not necessarily more genuine value creation

horizon_notes.6m: The outcome of the mandatory tender offer (SEC-approved 24 July 2026) will determine near-term free-float and ownership structure.
horizon_notes.1y: New ownership's stated intentions for the investment property (hold, develop, or sell) will likely be the primary driver of the stock's value, overshadowing quarterly FVTPL swings.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends entirely on what the new controlling shareholders choose to do with a Rs.1.4-1.85bn investment property inside a low-revenue holding shell -- outside this project's ability to forecast without further disclosure.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro, real-estate-market, or ownership-strategy data source in this project to assess a multi-year outcome for this shell/holding structure.

interim_updates.note_text: Industrial Asphalts (Ceylon) PLC (ASPH) reported Profit After Tax of Rs.16.19mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), up 323% YoY from Rs.3.82mn (Q1 FY2025/26), even as Revenue fell 9.0% YoY to Rs.12.61mn (2025: Rs.13.86mn). ASPH's former asphalt-manufacturing business has ceased; it is now an investment/property holding company whose 'Revenue' comprises only Rent Income from its Investment Property (Rs.11.70mn, +4.5% YoY from Rs.11.20mn), Interest Income on short-term investments (Rs.0.90mn, -33.5% YoY from Rs.1.36mn) and Dividend Income (nil this quarter vs Rs.1.31mn in Q1 FY2025/26) -- the revenue decline is entirely attributable to the absence of dividend income and lower interest income, not any weakening in the core rental line, which actually grew. The 323% PAT jump was driven almost entirely by mark-to-market swings on the Company's Financial Assets at FVTPL: Unrealized Gains on these assets rose to Rs.23.23mn (2025: Rs.10.88mn, +113.5%), while the Realized Loss on the same portfolio widened to Rs.3.74mn (2025: Rs.0.61mn loss, -510% i.e. more than 6x worse) -- netting to a total FVTPL gain of Rs.19.49mn versus Rs.10.27mn a year earlier, +89.9% YoY, which is the single largest driver of the quarter's profit growth and dwarfs the Rs.12.61mn revenue base. Administrative Expenses fell 9.0% YoY to Rs.14.12mn (2025: Rs.15.53mn), a genuine cost saving that also supported the 'Profit from Operating Activities' line, which rose 109% YoY to Rs.17.97mn (2025: Rs.8.60mn) -- note this subtotal already includes the FVTPL swings above, so it is not a like-for-like operating margin. Net Finance Charges eased 46.7% YoY to Rs.1.65mn (2025: Rs.3.10mn, only a net figure disclosed, no gross split), and Tax Expense fell 92.0% YoY to Rs.0.13mn (2025: Rs.1.67mn). Basic and diluted EPS were both Rs.0.004 (2025: Rs.0.001). Balance sheet at 30 June 2026: Total Assets Rs.1,619.79mn, 89% of which (Rs.1,447.0mn) is the Investment Property, carried at the Board's chosen (more conservative) KPMG leasehold valuation rather than an alternative Rs.1,850.0mn effectively-freehold valuation obtained from another valuer -- see Note 5. Total Equity was Rs.1,481.93mn (NAV/share Rs.0.47). Two subsequent events after quarter-end, outside these results but material to the stock: on 7 July 2026 Executive Director Mr. G Ramanan signed a binding agreement to sell his entire 48.03% stake (1,800,693,010 shares) to Arcasia Investment & Trading (Pvt) Ltd and ATX Partners (Pvt) Ltd, and a mandatory Rule 9 tender offer to all shareholders at Rs.0.40/share was approved by the SEC on 24 July 2026.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for ASPH, no prior quarter collected. The Statement of Financial Position's comparative column is 31 March 2026 (FY start), not 30 June 2025, so no YoY balance-sheet comparison (assets/liabilities/equity/working-capital items) is possible from this filing -- only the P&L (which does carry a genuine same-quarter YoY column) supports YoY analysis, hence yoy_json is limited to income-statement metrics. Net Finance Income/(Charges) is disclosed only as a single net line (no split of finance income vs finance costs), so those two fields are not populated. No segmental note is presented -- ASPH operates and reports as a single unsegmented entity (property/investment holding), so no segment-level attribution is possible or applicable, unlike diversified peers. trade_receivables/trade_payables/inventory/long_term_borrowings are genuine filing gaps in the sense that the Company simply has no trade operations generating these balances -- 'Receivables and Prepayments' is dominated by a related-party director advance, not trade debt, and there is no inventory or interest-bearing long-term loan on the balance sheet (only lease liabilities).
interim_updates.takeaway: ASPH's headline 323% YoY PAT growth to Rs.16.19mn is almost entirely a mark-to-market story: net gains on its Financial Assets at FVTPL portfolio rose to Rs.19.49mn (2025: Rs.10.27mn), a non-operating swing that exceeds the Company's entire Rs.12.61mn revenue base, while core revenue (rent, interest, dividends) actually fell 9.0% YoY on lost dividend and interest income. With administrative expenses down 9.0% and tax/finance costs both easing, the underlying cash-generative trend is less dramatic than the profit figure suggests -- and is now secondary in relevance to the 7 July 2026 binding sale of the Executive Director's 48.03% controlling stake and the subsequent SEC-approved mandatory tender offer at Rs.0.40/share, a change-of-control process that will likely dominate the stock's near-term narrative over these results.

Basic/Diluted Earnings per Share, Rs. (as disclosed, 3dp)

operational_highlights: Revenue Rs.12.61mn, -9.0% YoY (2025: Rs.13.86mn), driven by nil dividend income (2025: Rs.1.31mn) and interest income -33.5% YoY to Rs.0.90mn, partly offset by rent income +4.5% YoY to Rs.11.70mn.

PAT Rs.16.19mn, +323% YoY (2025: Rs.3.82mn), driven almost entirely by net FVTPL fair value gains of Rs.19.49mn vs Rs.10.27mn a year earlier (+89.9%): Unrealized Gain Rs.23.23mn (+113.5% YoY) partly offset by a widened Realized Loss of Rs.3.74mn (2025: Rs.0.61mn loss).
Administrative Expenses -9.0% YoY to Rs.14.12mn (2025: Rs.15.53mn); Net Finance Charges -46.7% YoY to Rs.1.65mn; Tax Expense -92.0% YoY to Rs.0.13mn.

Total Assets Rs.1,619.79mn at 30 June 2026, 89% represented by Investment Property carried at Rs.1,447.0mn (KPMG leasehold valuation, Board's conservative choice over an alternative Rs.1,850.0mn freehold-basis valuation). NAV/share Rs.0.47.

Subsequent to quarter-end: binding SPA (7 July 2026) for Executive Director Mr. G Ramanan to sell his full 48.03% stake; SEC-approved mandatory tender offer to all shareholders at Rs.0.40/share announced 24 July 2026 -- a change-of-control event not reflected in these results.
key_drivers: Net gain on Financial Assets at FVTPL (Unrealized Rs.23.23mn less Realized Loss Rs.3.74mn = Rs.19.49mn) vs Rs.10.27mn a year earlier, +89.9% YoY -- the dominant driver of the 323% PAT increase, exceeding total revenue of Rs.12.61mn.
Administrative Expenses -9.0% YoY to Rs.14.12mn, a genuine cost saving contributing to the 109% rise in 'Profit from Operating Activities'.
Revenue mix shift: loss of Rs.1.31mn dividend income and a 33.5% drop in interest income outweighed 4.5% rental growth, producing a 9.0% YoY revenue decline even as profit surged.
Tax Expense fell 92.0% YoY to Rs.0.13mn and Net Finance Charges fell 46.7% YoY to Rs.1.65mn, both aiding the flow-through from PBT (+196.9% YoY) to PAT (+323% YoY).
